explanation: Line 59 is PolFile.Load storing every entry read from a POL file under its dictionary key without looking at the name, so a loaded file can create the Configured, Queued for deletion and Key cleared states (and the **deletevalues / **deletekeys forms), not only Configured. The 'to: Configured' claim is false at this reach. Also fromStates is the string 'created' where the other transitions use state numbers: use the shape's way of saying creation. Rewrite as creation into each state the file's entries put a value in, or one transition naming the entry kinds. Add the creation of an empty store (PolicyLoader.vb 95-100 'New PolFile' + Save, PolicyLoader.vb 80-90 Null/'New PolFile', PolicySource.vb Duplicate) as creation into Not configured.

DeleteValue on a POL writes the **del. entry only when WillDeleteValue is still false after ForgetValue (line 94). From Key cleared (4) WillDeleteValue is true (line 124, any **delvals prefix), so nothing is written: state 4 is not a source of this transition, the value just stays deleted under the clearance. Remove 4 from fromStates (or say it writes nothing there). Also this is the POL implementation only: RegistryPolicyProxy.DeleteValue (PolicySource.vb 365-370) and RegFile.DeleteValue (RegFile.vb 233-240, writes an IsDeleter value) are separate writers; the lifecycle's state writtenAs says POL file only.

SetValue (105-109) only replaces the value entry; it removes neither a **del.<name> entry nor the **delvals. marker. So from Queued for deletion (3) the **del. entry stays in the file and Configured holds only because WillDeleteValue lines 130-131 let the later-sorting value entry override it; from Key cleared (4) the marker stays and is still written to the POL, so the result is cleared-and-configured, not a move out of state 4. State this precisely: the states are read from several entries together (the value entry plus **del./**delvals.), and a transition 'to Configured' from 3 or 4 leaves the earlier entry in place. Say what the person sees after saving.

ForgetValue is correct for [2,3]->1 but it is also what DeleteValue calls first (line 93), and it does not affect state 4 (it never removes **delvals.). Fine as stated, but note callers: PolicyProcessing.vb 260 and EditPol.vb 227 are the 'Forget' routes; make sure the evidence lines and the chain reach those, since the transition's meaning ('not configured, no deletion queued') differs from DeleteValue's.

ClearKey acts on a whole key (all its values), so the state is per key, not per value: the finding's lifecycle mixes per-value states (Configured, Queued for deletion) with a per-key state without saying so. Also, the system calls ClearKey then ForgetKeyClearance straight away (PolicyProcessing.vb 250-251, EditPol.vb 220-221), which purges values and leaves no marker, ending in Not configured, not Key cleared: the transition to Key cleared (4) is only the lasting one when ForgetKeyClearance does not follow (PolicyProcessing.vb 330, 364, EditPol.vb 179-182). ClearKey from state 4 throws on Entries.Add of a duplicate (line 188), so excluding 4 is right; say so. Add the purge path as a transition to 1 or explain it in the state text.

ForgetKeyClearance removes every entry starting with **delvals (so also the MS '**delvals' form), not only '**delvals.'; the state's writtenAs names only the dotted form. Fix the state's writtenAs to both forms, as line 124 and 192 test.

Three gaps in the states. (1) Queued for deletion is claimed as '**del.<name>' only, yet the code treats a **deletevalues entry (semicolon-separated names, line 126-129) as a deletion for each listed value and ApplyDifference deletes them (lines 157-159); and Key cleared is claimed as '**delvals.' only, yet '**delvals' and '**deletekeys' (lines 124, 160-167) are also acted on. These arrive via Load of MS POL files. Name them or say why not. (2) The lifecycle ignores the third IPolicySource store that records states: RegFile (REG file, 'Entries' there are RegFileKey/RegFileValue with IsDeleter true = deletion, key IsDeleter = cleared; RegFile.vb 218-252). Its Configured / Queued / Key cleared are written by SetValue/DeleteValue/ClearKey there and saved at RegFile.vb 183; the fields 'stateFields' do not list them. (3) The registry store never holds states 3 or 4: say that deletion/clearing are applied at once there (RegistryPolicyProxy.ForgetValue and ClearKey 371-373, 416-420 simply delete), and that PolicyLoader.Save for LocalGpo without the infrastructure applies POL queued deletions/clearances immediately to the registry via ApplyDifference (PolicyLoader.vb 127-131).

says: Transitions made by RegistryPolicyProxy are missing for ForgetValue (PolicySource.vb 371-373, calls DeleteValue: Configured -> Not configured) and ClearKey (416-420, deletes every top-level value of the key through ForgetValue: Configured -> Not configured for all values of the key). Only DeleteValue and SetValue are recorded for the registry. Add the two, or one transition each, with the callers that reach them (PolicyProcessing.vb 260, 250, 330, 364; PolicySource.vb ApplyDifference 150-175 when PolicyLoader.Save applies a POL to the registry, PolicyLoader.vb 127-131).

RegFile is an IPolicySource target for ApplyDifference (REG export: ExportReg.vb 28-29, Main.vb 748-ish) and records the three change kinds: SetValue (RegFile.vb 218-228) writes a value, DeleteValue (231-238) writes an IsDeleter value, ClearKey (240-244) replaces the key with an IsDeleter key; ForgetKeyClearance (246-251) removes it. The job's save at RegFile.vb 183 persists these, but no transition covers them and the receipt skips them. Add transitions (or say they are the same states in an export file, and that ForgetValue/ContainsValue throw NotImplementedException), and note REG import (ImportReg.vb 39, RegFile.Apply 254-268) feeds POL/registry sources through the other transitions.

The saves PolicyLoader.vb 180-205 (UpdateGptIni) change the Group Policy version stamp, which the entity's purpose names as part of the setting, and PolicyLoader.vb 95-100 creates an empty POL file. The job's receipt lists them but no record says what they do to the life: write that UpdateGptIni adds 1 (machine) or 0x10000 (user) to Version (lines 187-191) or writes Version=65537 when absent or the file is new, never a state change, and that the 95-100 save creates a store with no entries (every setting Not configured). Without that a reader cannot tell the stamp is outside the states, nor that the stamp only moves on LocalGpo/SidGpo saves (PolicyLoader.vb 119-124, 143-145) and not on PolFile, NtUserDat or LocalRegistry saves.
